arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 3/5 — Today the first real conversation (agronomy, her grandmother) and she agrees to see Moshe after Shabbat. Next: she visits Moshe, Saturday night Nov 7.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 1/3 — Watered less, but the leaves are going dry and Ishai keeps plucking them. Dana's house call is Saturday night.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: New. Sababa Creative's chickpea client wants it friendlier by Sunday morning. Today Ishai asks Gadi about the fee and finds the idea: eyes.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: She missed the cafe and the bar on Nov 4. Tonight she apologises by text and comes for Shabbat dinner Friday, with wine.

arcs.title: Falafel the dog
arcs.stage: Settled in; walks, naps by the desk, goes along to the cafe. Mrs. Levi objects to his nails.

arcs.title: The wider circle
arcs.stage: Tomer back in the picture tonight and on to Dana. Kobi's lottery system continues. Mr. Zelig gives accidental design advice.

beats.goal: Gadi phones from Sababa Creative about the chickpea logo Ishai has been redrawing since yesterday: the client wants to see it by Sunday. Gadi is never seen, only heard. Ishai tries to ask for more money and half manages it, remembering what Noa keeps telling him.
beats.forceText: Ishai takes a call from Gadi at his desk, the chickpea logo open on the laptop.

forceLines.say: The chickpea client wants it by Sunday, Ishai.
Sunday. Sure. We should talk about the fee.

forceCommentary.say: He said the word fee out loud. Mark the calendar.
Noa is rubbing off on him. Finally, a spine.

moments.text: Ishai's phone buzzes beside the laptop, the chickpea logo open on the screen. He answers Gadi standing up, as if that helps.

lines.say: Ishai, my friend. Tell me the chickpea is finished.
The chickpea is close. It has a good stroke weight now.
The client doesn't know what a stroke weight is. They want to see it Sunday.
Sunday morning or Sunday evening?
Morning. And they asked if it can look friendlier.
It's a chickpea, Gadi. How friendly should it get?
Friendly enough that they pay us.
About that. This is the fourth round. We should talk about the fee.
The fee. Since when do you talk about the fee?
Since I have a dog to feed.

commentary.say: He used the dog as a negotiating tactic. Falafel should ask for a percentage.
Fee talk before nine. Who is this man?

moments.text: Ishai paces to the windowsill with the phone, looks at Moshe, and comes back to the desk.

lines.say: Okay. Finish it by Sunday and I'll see what I can do.
What you can do is a number, Gadi. I'd like a number.
You've been talking to Noa.
Everyone's been talking to Noa. She doesn't answer, though.
I'll send you the brief again, with the friendly notes.
There are notes about friendliness?
Two pages. Sunday morning, Ishai.
Sunday morning. And a number.

commentary.say: She didn't show at the cafe or the bar. He noticed. He is hurt.
Two pages of notes for one chickpea. Moshe got less attention at birth.

beats.goal: Ishai walks to Cafe Nahat with Falafel for a real coffee, the one he skipped yesterday when he waited for Noa. He has been plucking dry leaves off Moshe and doesn't know if that is good. Their first real conversation: Dana asks about him for once, and when he describes the leaves she says she'd have to see the plant herself. It is almost an invitation; they agree she'll come by after Shabbat. Lior types nearby. Not a date, and neither calls it one.
beats.forceText: At the counter of Cafe Nahat Ishai describes Moshe's dry leaves. Dana stops wiping the machine and listens.

forceLines.say: Dry leaves can mean anything. I'd have to see him.

forceCommentary.say: SHE'S MAKING A HOUSE CALL. Somebody open a window.
Moshe has a specialist now. His insurance is excellent.

moments.text: Ishai comes to the counter with Falafel at his heels. Dana already has the extra shot going; he watches the cup instead of his phone.

lines.say: Yesterday you drank ice water and left. Today you want coffee?
Yesterday I was waiting for someone. She didn't come.
Noa.
Noa. I'm not worried. I'm mildly offended.
Sit. It's quiet for ten minutes.
Moshe's leaves are going dry at the edges. I've been plucking them off.
Bottom leaves or top leaves?
Is there a right answer? Tell me the right answer.
There's no answer from here. I'd have to see him.
See him. You mean, come over? To see Moshe.
To see the plant, Ishai. Don't make that face.

commentary.say: She said she'd see him. Zero blushing allowed. I'm blushing.
A professional consultation at last. Moshe has waited for this all season.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the end of the counter with his cup. Dana leans on the machine for a moment, which she never does; behind them Lior types.

lines.say: Why design? You don't seem to like it.
I like it until someone says friendlier. Nobody ever asks me that.
Asks you what?
Why. Why anything. Why coffee, in your case?
I was going to study agronomy. Then my grandmother got sick and I stayed.
I'm sorry. And now?
Now I draw leaves on cups for men who take three weeks to notice.
That's fair. When would you, for Moshe?
After Shabbat. Saturday night, if the plant's still alive.
He'll be alive. I'll tell him.

commentary.say: AGRONOMY. A dream. A sick grandmother. I need a tissue and a wedding planner.
He's going to tell the basil. I respect the chain of command.

beats.goal: Ishai takes a break from the chickpea and walks Falafel to the park to clear his head. On the way past the pond he meets Mr. Zelig, who is explaining something to the pigeons. A short odd exchange: Zelig takes to Falafel, and without meaning to says something useful about friendliness. Ishai thinks about the logo differently afterwards.
beats.forceText: By the pond, Mr. Zelig stops talking to the pigeons and looks down at Falafel.

forceLines.say: This one listens. The pigeons only pretend.

forceCommentary.say: Zelig's audience just grew by one dog. Ratings are up.
Finally a man who understands pigeons. Next to nobody asked.

moments.text: Falafel pulls toward the pond, where Mr. Zelig stands among the pigeons with his hands behind his back, talking quietly. He stops and looks down at the dog.

lines.say: This one listens. The pigeons only pretend.
He's mostly listening for food. Sorry, he doesn't bother them much.
Everyone is listening for food, young man. What do you do?
I draw logos. Right now, a chickpea. It has to look friendlier.
A chickpea doesn't want your friendship.
I'll tell the client.
Why is a dog friendly? He looks at you. That's all.
So it needs to look at people.
I was speaking to the pigeons. Good afternoon.

commentary.say: Free design direction from a man who bills in breadcrumbs.
He just took notes from Mr. Zelig. Gadi could never.

moments.text: Ishai walks the path back with Falafel on the leash, drawing a small circle in the air with one finger, then a dot inside it.

lines.say: Eyes. It just needs eyes. Falafel, you're a genius and so is that lunatic.

commentary.say: Two dots saved the whole account. Art school is a scam.
The dog found a napkin yesterday and an idea today. Promotions are coming.

beats.goal: Coming back up, Ishai meets Mrs. Levi in the corridor. She complains about crumbs and the dog's nails on the stairs, then asks if he is alone for Shabbat tomorrow, and hands him soup. She has seen Noa going up and down all week and has theories. He says a friend may come, and that someone is coming to look at the basil on Saturday night. She will now be watching the corridor.
beats.forceText: Mrs. Levi catches Ishai at his door with a pot of soup and a list of complaints.

forceLines.say: You're thin. And your dog walks like a typewriter.
Thank you, Mrs. Levi. For the soup, I mean.

forceCommentary.say: She insults him and feeds him. That's the whole of Jewish love.
The corridor has a security system. It wears slippers.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi's door opens the second Ishai reaches the top of the stairs. She holds a small pot in both hands and looks at Falafel's paws.

lines.say: Your dog walks like a typewriter. All day. Tak tak tak.
Good afternoon, Mrs. Levi. I can cut his nails.
You're thin. Take this. It's only chicken.
Thank you. You didn't have to.
That girl with the drawings on her arms. Three times yesterday, up and down.
That's Noa. She's a friend. She brings pastries.
I found the crumbs. Tomorrow is Shabbat. You'll be alone?
Maybe Noa, if she remembers. I haven't heard from her.
And Saturday night? I hear things through the wall.
Someone's coming to look at Moshe. The basil. A plant person.
A plant person. Wear a clean shirt.

commentary.say: Mrs. Levi knows. She has always known. Protect her at all costs.
She hears Saturday night through the wall on a Thursday. Remarkable hardware.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the table with Mrs. Levi's soup, Falafel watching every spoon. Moshe is on the windowsill behind him.

lines.say: Okay, Moshe. Saturday night. Try to look like you've been eating well.

commentary.say: Moshe has two days to get his affairs in order.
Soup from one woman, a house call from another. He's thriving.

beats.goal: Ishai's first beginners' improv lesson with Yael at the back of The Black Candle, Thursdays at 17:00, paid for by Noa as four lessons. He is awkward and over-apologizes, says no to a made-up scene, and learns 'yes, and'. A pretend shop gets him to name a price and hold it, which echoes his fee with Gadi. Yael sets him one bit of homework.
beats.forceText: At the back of The Black Candle Yael stands the beginners' improv class in a circle, and Ishai takes his place.

forceLines.say: Ishai? Noa paid for four lessons. She said you'd ask for a refund.
I was going to ask very politely.

forceCommentary.say: He's been signed up by his own best friend. This is what friendship looks like.
Four lessons, prepaid. Noa has more faith in him than his clients do.

moments.text: Just before five Ishai steps into the back of The Black Candle, where chairs stand in a circle. Yael, the improv teacher, ticks his name off a list.

lines.say: Ishai? Noa paid for four lessons. She said you'd ask for a refund.
I was going to ask very politely.
It's five o'clock, so no refunds. Bag down, phone away.
What if a client calls?
Then the client gets to wait. Have you ever done this?
I once said yes to a logo in the dark.
Good, that counts. First rule. Whatever your partner says is true.
And if it's wrong?
It's still true. You say yes, and you add something.
I already say yes to everyone. That's my whole problem.

commentary.say: He's been signed up by his own best friend. This is what friendship looks like.
Four lessons, prepaid. Noa has more faith in him than his clients do.

moments.text: The class stands in a circle for the warm-up. Yael claps, and they pass a sound around the ring; Ishai's turn arrives before he is ready.

lines.say: Pass the clap to whoever you're looking at. Don't plan it.
Who am I looking at? Am I looking at you?
You're looking at the floor.
The floor and I have a good relationship.
Again. Eyes up. Don't apologize when it goes wrong.
Sorry.
That's one. Every sorry costs you a push-up.
Is that part of the method?
No. I just made it up. That's the method.
Sorry. No. Not sorry. How many is that?

commentary.say: He apologized for apologizing. That's advanced work for a beginner.
Keep the push-ups going, he owes the gym anyway.

moments.text: Yael pairs up with Ishai for the first scene, two chairs facing the class. She decides they are astronauts and he has to go along with it.

lines.say: Commander, the ship is out of hummus.
No, I think we have some left in the...
Stop. Clap. What did you just do?
I checked the fridge. Sorry. That's two.
You said no. Try again. The hummus, Commander.
Yes. And we've been eating the logo.
The logo? Which logo?
The chickpea. It was friendlier before we ate it.
There it is. Did you hear that? That came from somewhere.
That came from Sunday morning.

commentary.say: A chickpea in space. He cannot get away from that client.
He said no to a pretend astronaut. If only he'd try it on Gadi.

moments.text: One more scene: Yael plays a customer and Ishai a shopkeeper. She tells him he can only win by naming his price and not backing down.

lines.say: This chair is lovely. How much?
For you? Whatever you think is fair.
Clap. Name a price.
Fifty shekels.
Fifty? That's a lot for a chair.
You're right, forty. Thirty. Take it.
Clap. I said one word and you lost twenty shekels.
You said it with a very convincing face.
Again. Fifty. Now what do you say?
Yes, it's fifty. And it's a good chair.
And?
And I'm not sorry. Is that three?

commentary.say: Oh, that is the fee conversation with a chair in it. She has no idea.
Fifty shekels and he held on. Gadi, you may want to sit down.

moments.text: The class ends with the chairs back in place and the first evening customers at the bar. Yael hands Ishai a folded sheet with next week's exercise.

lines.say: Not bad. You're funny when you stop checking the fridge.
I felt like a man falling down stairs.
That's the first lesson. Everyone falls. Next Thursday at five.
Is there homework?
Yes. Once this week, don't say sorry to someone who should be saying it to you.
That's a very specific homework.
Noa told me a few things.
Noa talks too much.
Yes, and?
Yes, and she's paying. See you Thursday.

commentary.say: Homework that goes straight at Gadi. I love this teacher.
Three more lessons paid. Ishai, you may never be the same man.

beats.goal: Ishai meets Tomer at The Black Candle, his loud friend since school, who has finished a job nearby. Noa finally texts: an apology for not turning up at the cafe and the bar, and she'll come for Shabbat dinner tomorrow. Tomer teases him about the plant person and asks to see the chickpea. Kobi, getting tipsy, joins in at the end. Ishai goes home by 22:30; he has a logo to finish.
beats.forceText: Ishai and Tomer share a corner of The Black Candle. Ishai's phone lights up with Noa's name.

forceLines.say: Who's texting you? You smiled. You never smile.
Noa. She's alive, and she's bringing wine tomorrow.

forceCommentary.say: Noa's back, Shabbat is on, and Dana comes after. Pace yourself, Ishai.
Tomer speaks at a volume Moshe can hear from home.

moments.text: The Black Candle is half full. Tomer, still in his work boots, pushes a beer across the table; Ishai's phone lights up with a text.

lines.say: Noa. Finally. She says the studio swallowed her.
Who gets swallowed by a studio? She owes you a beer.
She has a client doing a whole back. She's coming tomorrow for Shabbat. With wine.
You smiled. Why are you smiling? You never smile.
I'm relieved. I thought she was mad at me.
No. There's something else. Who is it?
Nobody. Someone's coming over Saturday to look at my basil.
Look at your basil. Ishai. Is that what they call it now?
She's a barista, Tomer. She knows about plants.
Twenty years I know you. You've never had a woman look at anything.

commentary.say: Tomer got it out of him in four lines. Why isn't he on our show?
Look at your basil. I will not be taking questions.

message.say: Sorry Ishush, the studio swallowed me, big back piece. Shabbat tomorrow? I'll bring wine and an excuse.

moments.text: Tomer heads to the bar for another round. Kobi, a little loose already, drops into his seat and looks at the logo on Ishai's phone.

lines.say: What's that? Is that a potato?
It's a chickpea. It needs eyes. I just drew them today.
It's looking at me. I don't like how it's looking at me.
That's friendly. It's meant to be friendly.
That's what they said about my brother-in-law.
Do you know you're sitting in Tomer's chair?
Tomer who? Lottery's Saturday night. I've got a system.
You had a system yesterday too.
Yesterday was testing. Hey, buy a ticket. For the chickpea.

commentary.say: First user testing of the logo. The results are concerning.
A tipsy man fears a chickpea. Gadi, that's your campaign.
